transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~1h14m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Flores (Redwood Partner Ops), Samir Rao (ClearBridge CTO), Priya Nair (ClearBridge Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (ClearBridge Procurement)

Optional summary: quick pipeline triage between Redwood and ClearBridge to map which accounts/POCs we co-sell, align on private deployment constraints, and surface operational risks for a near-term pilot.

Topics: co-sell motion, pilot scope, data residency and VPC/on-prem constraints, SLAs and fallbacks, partner revenue split and lead routing, timeline and procurement gating.

[00:00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, welcome, thanks for making time. quick intros, I think everyone on the call knows each other but we'll do quick 10 second intros.
[00:00:12] Samir (CTO): Samir Rao, CTO at ClearBridge, we're the payer-provider integration team, we own inference in prod for claims routing.
[00:00:18] Priya (Head of ML): Priya Nair, leading ML infra and model ops. lots of constraints around PHI residency.
[00:00:21] Lena (Procurement): Lena Ortiz, procurement. I'll be shepherding contract language and timelines.
[00:00:27] Alex (AE): Awesome. Maya, Diego from our side?
[00:00:30] Maya (SE): Maya Patel, solutions eng, I'll own the technical checks and the bench.
[00:00:33] Diego (Partner Ops): Diego Flores, partner ops — I'll help with the co-sell rules, revenue motion and deal routing to our channel team.
[00:00:40] Alex (AE): Cool, agenda: 1) map the pilot scope and success metrics, 2) discuss ClearBridge constraints (VPC / on‑prem / data residency), 3) flag operational risks and fallback plans, 4) next steps — pricing and procurement runway. sound ok?
[00:00:52] Samir (CTO): Yep. high level: we need a pilot for claims triage with <100ms p95 target for single-turn inference and batch rerank overnight. cost is sensitive; we've seen spikes with other vendors.
[00:01:07] Priya (Head of ML): to add, model size matters because of memory limits on our clusters; we prefer 16-bit quantized models if quality isn't dropped. also need audit logs for every token-level call.
[00:01:19] Maya (SE): got it — we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated for p95 SLAs, but for PHI we have Private VPC or on-prem options. there's a tradeoff: Dedicated gives predictable throughput but data passes through our control plane unless you choose Private where logs can be customer-managed.
[00:01:36] Samir (CTO): can you clarify difference between dedicated and private again? we've seen those terms mixed.
[00:01:40] Maya (SE): sure — Dedicated means reserved GPU pools in Redwood's infra dedicated to you; the tenancy is isolated but the control plane is hosted. Private means we deploy a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem, you own the control plane, keys, and audit logs — better for HIPAA/PHI.
[00:01:58] Priya (Head of ML): that Private option is interesting. but we have strict KMS controls, HSM preference. whats the KMS integration look like?
[00:02:06] Diego (Partner Ops): from the partner side, we can route the deal as a co-sell where Redwood is the vendor and we share revenue. the channel legal packet handles KMS SLAs usually. but we'll need legal to review HSM integrations.
[00:02:17] Lena (Procurement): timeline: we need procurement check-off in 6 weeks if pilot goes ahead — internal security review takes about 2 weeks plus legal redlines.
[00:02:26] Alex (AE): noted. quick qualification: what's your existing stack? where does this sit — AWS, GCP?
[00:02:31] Samir (CTO): primarily AWS, EKS clusters, some on-prem for legacy. data stores in us-east-1, cannot leave region for PHI.
[00:02:40] Maya (SE): Redwood supports region pinning for Private and Dedicated, and we can ensure compute stays in us-east-1. small caveat: if you want on-prem we'll need an engineer to scope network.
[00:02:51] Priya (Head of ML): also curious on caching and KV for prompt context; we have long chat histories — want to avoid repeated token costs.
[00:02:58] Maya (SE): we have prefix/KV caching and can keep hot contexts in-memory on the pods. cost/latency tradeoffs: larger cache reduces token regen but increases memory footprint. we'll show numbers in the bench.
[00:03:09] Samir (CTO): security questions: SOC2? iso? audit logs retention?
[00:03:12] Alex (AE): Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we have ISO planned next quarter. audit log retention configurable; for Private you control retention. we'll send security pack (link).
[00:03:24] Priya (Head of ML): good. any customers using your private control plane for PHI workloads in production?
[00:03:28] Maya (SE): yes, a healthcare payer we can reference — we'll include contact references in the pack (redacted).
[00:03:35] Diego (Partner Ops): from partner motion — partner should be involved in the sales deck and will be on the SOW. we propose a joint 6–8 week pilot: week 1 scoping, week 2 infra setup, week 3 bench runs, week 4 fine-tuning, weeks 5–6 evaluation and go/no-go.
[00:03:51] Samir (CTO): that's reasonable. procurement gating might add extra 1–2 weeks.
[00:03:55] Lena (Procurement): yes expect legal redlines. Also we need clear liability language around PHI — indemnity and breach response windows.
[00:04:04] Alex (AE): we'll flag legal — Diego can pull partner legal templates and Maya will note the technical requirements for SOW.
[00:04:12] Maya (SE): technical risk flags I want to call out: 1) p95 <100ms might be hard for larger context sizes on smaller GPU classes, 2) on-prem network egress and firewall rules can add jitter, 3) quantization can affect model quality — we should baseline with your prompt sets.
[00:04:28] Priya (Head of ML): what GPU classes do you recommend for this workload? we currently have 8 vCPU nodes with up to 64GB RAM on our clusters.
[00:04:37] Maya (SE): for single-turn low-latency we typically recommend A10G class or equivalent; for higher quality and larger context M60 / H100s would be ideal. Dedicated can be provisioned with these; Private on-prem we can support similar hardware if you provide nodes.
[00:04:51] Samir (CTO): cost question: how do you price dedicated vs private vs hosted? our budget cap is tight for the pilot.
[00:04:58] Alex (AE): short answer: hosted (pay-as-you-go) is per-token; Dedicated is a reserved monthly for capacity (cheaper per-unit when utilized); Private has licensing + infra cost. We'll share a joint pricing grid. For pilots we usually do a blended discount.
[00:05:12] Diego (Partner Ops): partner co-sell economics: we can agree to referral splits for the first N months, then full contract revenue share — we will put numbers in the one-pager.
[00:05:20] Samir (CTO): important: can Redwood or partner ingest PHI for tuning? we cannot send raw PHI to external parties.
[00:05:27] Maya (SE): for that we recommend either on-prem Private or using redaction with local KMS. there's a workflow for secure fine-tuning where data never leaves customer storage and we run training in their VPC. we'll document options.
[00:05:40] Priya (Head of ML): ok, so pilot scoping: we want to test two paths — 1) small-hosted trial to validate accuracy and cost, with synthetic redacted dataset, 2) Private VPC pilot for production-like latency and PHI handling.
[00:05:52] Alex (AE): nice, that dual-track approach reduces risk and moves faster. we'll propose that in the SOW.
[00:05:57] Lena (Procurement): from timeline POV, hosted trial could start fastest; Private will require security sign-off which is why we need your checklist.
[00:06:05] Diego (Partner Ops): operational escalation play: if latency SLOs fail, Redwood's router can fallback to a smaller model or different region; we should document fallback decision trees in the runbook.
[00:06:16] Maya (SE): yes fallback is critical — we can keep a lower-cost model as a warm standby. note that quality will vary.
[00:06:22] Samir (CTO): any competitors we should watch — we've run pilots with OpenAI and Anthropic; they had unpredictable throttling during spikes.
[00:06:29] Alex (AE): noted — we'll include reliability comparatives (anonymized).
[00:06:34] Priya (Head of ML): bench specifics — we'll measure p50/p95, token cost per request, and QA pass rate against current rule-based engine. need to confirm the test prompt set.
[00:06:45] Maya (SE): please upload a canonical set of prompts (10–15) and sample logs. we'll prepare a perf matrix.
[00:06:51] Samir (CTO): action: Priya will drop sample prompt set in shared drive by Friday.
[00:06:55] Alex (AE): I'll capture that.
[00:06:59] (brief cross talk)
[00:07:10] Maya (SE): operational detail: for Private we need node capacity and network CIDR ranges, and a list of allowed egress endpoints for our support tunnels.
[00:07:20] Priya (Head of ML): ok we'll get that to you.
[00:07:23] Lena (Procurement): procurement question: do you require a minimum contract term for Dedicated?
[00:07:27] Alex (AE): yes Dedicated typically has monthly or annual reserved commitments; pilot can be structured as a short-term pilot with a rollback clause. we'll work on flexible language.
[00:07:36] Samir (CTO): what about telemetry and traces — we need per-token tracing and correlation to request IDs.
[00:07:42] Maya (SE): we emit token-level metrics and request IDs; for Private you can ingest logs directly into your ELK-stack or S3. Hosted we push to our dashboard but you can export.
[00:07:53] Priya (Head of ML): good. are there throttles we should know about? bursts?
[00:07:58] Maya (SE): Dedicated gives deterministic throughput; Hosted is rate-limited and can throttle under extreme spikes; Private depends on your infra. we'll model expected QPS in the bench.
[00:08:09] Diego (Partner Ops): on go-to-market: we should do a joint exec briefing after pilot completion to show value and get sponsor buy-in. partner can bring a customer reference.
[00:08:18] Alex (AE): agree. ok let's recap next steps then items.
[00:08:22] Alex (AE): recap: Redwood to send co-sell one-pager + pricing grid (Alex/Diego). Redwood SE (Maya) to produce benchmark plan and target perf matrix. ClearBridge (Priya) to share prompt set and metrics. Lena to confirm procurement constraints and timeline. schedule SE bench the week of 10/26.
[00:08:41] Priya (Head of ML): yes will upload prompts and p95 snapshots.
[00:08:44] Lena (Procurement): I'll confirm timeline and PO language by 10/22.
[00:08:48] Diego (Partner Ops): I'll send partner legal template and proposed revenue split by 10/15.
[00:08:54] Alex (AE): perfect. any other open risks?
[00:08:57] Samir (CTO): only the HSM/KMS and p95 performance for large contexts.
[00:09:03] Maya (SE): we'll call those out in the bench and SOW.
[00:09:07] Alex (AE): thanks all. we'll follow up with minutes and updated action items.

(End of captured transcript — remaining ~65 minutes were Q&A and technical deep dive details between Maya and Priya on exact perf tuning parameters; sections below are excerpted highlights.)

[00:20:12] Maya (SE): when you say 100ms p95 are you counting network RTT?
[00:20:16] Priya (Head of ML): yes, that's application end-to-end, including our service-to-service hop.
[00:20:22] Maya (SE): ok that'll push us toward collocating infra or private deployment in the same AZ; we should test inter-AZ latency.
[00:20:30] Samir (CTO): can you run synthetic with our proxy in the loop?
[00:20:33] Maya (SE): yes, we'll script a test harness that includes your network hop.

[00:37:40] Maya (SE): quantization note — 8-bit quant will save memory but we need to baseline quality on the sample prompts. we'll log hallucination delta.

[00:55:05] Alex (AE): final note on co-sell ops: we'll set up a shared SFDC opportunity and track influence. Diego will own partner reporting.
